chapters.about: Genesis 15:3, Eliezer inheriting, physical vs spiritual legacy

chapters.about: Vehe'emin b'Hashem, Bameh eda, merit of the korbanot

chapters.title: The Animals of Berit Ben HaBetarim
chapters.about: Three calves, goats, rams, turtle dove, pigeon, and their sacrificial hints

chapters.title: Splitting the Halves and Treaty Customs
chapters.about: Passing between pieces, why birds were not split, representation of nations vs Israel

summary: This class examines Genesis Chapter 15 through the commentary of Rashi, focusing on Avram's longing for an heir and Hashem's promise of countless descendants. It analyzes the explanations of Avram being shown the stars from above the cosmos and stepping beyond his astrological destiny. The discussion continues into the Covenant Between the Parts (Berit Ben HaBetarim), detailing the symbolism of the animals, their connection to future sacrifices, and the prophetic imagery of Israel and the nations.
questions: Why did Avram ask for a sign regarding the Land of Israel if he believed Hashem regarding having children?
What does Rashi mean when stating that Hashem took Avram 'outside' to view the stars?
How does changing a person's Hebrew name affect their Mazal?
What do the different animals in the Covenant Between the Parts symbolize according to Rashi?
Why were the heifer, goat, and ram split in two while the birds remained whole?
